title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}.

- 𝔊̂^+_{0,3} is the profinite Teichmüller group of type (0,3), essentially the free profinite group on two generators a and b.
- M'^~_{0,3} is a profinite 'modular' extension 1 → 𝔊̂^+_{0,3} → M'^~_{0,3} → Γ'^~_Q → 1.
- Γ'^~_Q is the group cut out by the (flattened) lacet equations, a GT-hat-like replacement for Gal(Q̄/Q).
- φ = Ψ_𝔊 : 𝔊̂^+_{0,3} → 𝔊 is a surjection onto a finite group; it is a dessin d'enfant given by its monodromy group with generators ρ = φ(a), σ = φ(b).
- On the preceding page (517) Grothendieck states a theorem. For an 'effective' surjection φ there is a unique homomorphism φ_M from M'^~_{0,3} to a finite 'modular' group M°_φ. It is characterised by acting on the elements u_{α,β,f} (built from parameters satisfying the flattened lacet equations) through the invariants φ(α), φ(β), φ(f). This gives a morphism of exact sequences 1→𝔊̂→M'^~→Γ'^~→1 ⟶ 1→𝔊→M°_φ→Γ°_φ→1.

This page: making φ_M explicit. Grothendieck says φ_M amounts to the data of three homomorphisms.
- (73) Ψ_{T_ρ} : Γ'^~_Q → T_ρ and Ψ_{T_σ} : Γ'^~_Q → T_σ. Here T_ρ, T_σ are finite groups attached to the cyclic data of ρ and σ: plausibly groups recording the exponent λ mod ord(ρ) and conjugation data, called Z_ρ, Z_σ on the next page. A margin note says ρ, σ stand for ρ_𝔊, σ_𝔊 in indices.
- (74) Ψ_G : M'^~_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}. G_{ρ,σ} is a finite group containing the image of 𝔊; the next page says G_{ρ,σ} = B_{ρ,σ}·𝔊, so it is presumably a subgroup of a semidirect product of 𝔊 by automorphisms preserving the generator data.
- (75)–(77) Compatibility condition. For x in M'^~ with image ẋ in Γ'^~, set a = Ψ_{T_ρ}(ẋ), b = Ψ_{T_σ}(ẋ), U = Ψ_G(x). Then δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b) = δ_G(U) in a common finite quotient γ_{ρ,σ}. Equivalently the three composites M'^~ → γ_{ρ,σ} coincide, so (Ψ_{T_ρ}∘can, Ψ_{T_σ}∘can, Ψ_G) lands in the fibre product T_ρ ×_γ T_σ ×_γ G_{ρ,σ}. Most plausibly γ_{ρ,σ} is a cyclotomic quotient (Ẑ^* reduced mod a common modulus): the cyclotomic exponent λ read off through ρ, through σ and through 𝔊 must agree.
- (78) Ψ_G restricted to 𝔊̂^+_{0,3} equals Ψ_𝔊 = φ.
- (79)–(80) Equivariance: for x in M'^~ with U = Ψ_G(x), we have φ ∘ int(x)|𝔊̂ = int(U)|𝔊 ∘ φ. So Ψ_G is a lift of the outer action to a genuine action on the finite quotient 𝔊, compatible with conjugation.

Purpose. This is the finite-level, explicit description of how the Galois/GT-type group acts on a single dessin, i.e. on the finite group 𝔊 with its marked generating pair. Page 519 recasts the construction as a functoriality statement under further surjections 𝔊 → 𝔊'.
errors: Notation drifts. Page 517 calls the maps φ_𝔊 and φ_M; this page calls them Ψ_𝔊 and Ψ_G. The source of the map is written M'^~_{0,3} on this page and M'^~_{0,3} on 517, but its target is G_{ρ,σ} here versus M°_φ on 517. Presumably G_{ρ,σ} is the 'G-component' of M°_φ; this identification is not stated.

The groups T_ρ, T_σ, γ_{ρ,σ} and G_{ρ,σ} and the maps δ are defined on earlier pages and not recalled here. Whether the triple determines φ_M bijectively (the 'i.e.' in (77)) cannot be checked from this page alone.
In the struck-out line Grothendieck first wrote b = Ψ_{T_ρ}(ẏ). He corrected this in (75) to b = Ψ_{T_σ}(ẋ), so it is a self-corrected slip.

ideas.what: Explicit finite-level description of the action of a GT/Galois-type group on a two-generated finite quotient (a dessin) of the free profinite group. The action is given as a homomorphism from the profinite extension to a finite group lifting the quotient map and intertwining conjugations.
ideas.modern_name: GT-hat action on dessins / finite quotients; GT(G)-type finite approximations of GT-hat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for GT-hat; Lochak–Schneps for GT actions on dessins; P. Guillot (2010s) for systematic finite-group 'GT-shadows' / action on pairs of generators; Kalugin–Dolgushev for GT-shadows
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Galois action on dessins; this explicit finite construction is not there

ideas.what: Compatibility of cyclotomic data read from the two generators and from the whole group: the three composites to γ_{ρ,σ} must be equal (fibre-product condition).
ideas.modern_name: Consistency of the cyclotomic character λ mod orders of the generators (the λ-component of GT-hat at finite level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld / Ihara (χ-component of GT); finite-level versions by Guillot, Dolgushev et al.

ideas.what: Equivariance diagram (80): Ψ intertwines int(x) on the profinite group with int(U) on the finite quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting an outer Galois action to an action on a characteristic or stable quotient

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds, for each two-generated finite quotient (𝔊; ρ, σ) of the free profinite group, a finite 'modular' target group fibred over cyclotomic data (T_ρ, T_σ, γ_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ}). This is the finite-level shadow of the GT/Galois action, and page 519 makes it functorial in 𝔊. It closely anticipates Guillot's finite groups attached to pairs of generators and the 'GT-shadows' of Dolgushev and collaborators (2020s), which approximate GT-hat through finite quotients and generator pairs.
missed.quote: δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b) = δ_G(U) dans γ_{ρ,σ} ... i.e. les trois homomorphismes ... sont égaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedent for the finite-quotient approach to GT-hat (GT-shadows). The specific fibre-product packaging over a cyclotomic quotient γ_{ρ,σ}, with T_ρ and T_σ, may be worth comparing with modern definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step in an unpublished construction. It recasts the Galois/GT-type action on a dessin's monodromy group as a compatible triple of homomorphisms into finite groups. It is conceptually close to later work (Guillot, GT-shadows) that is not credited to Grothendieck, but the page itself is mostly bookkeeping of diagrams.
transcription_corrections: The transcription's page numbers 562/563 for the neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's own numbering; the archive page number at the bottom is 518 for this page.
In (78) the image reads Ψ_G | 𝔊̂^+_{0,3} = Ψ_𝔊; the transcription has this right, though the symbol after '=' resembles Ψ with a gothic G.
In (75) the word 'Soit' is crossed out with 'G' beneath, giving roughly 'Soit_G' → the δ_G reading. The line then reads: a = Ψ_{T_ρ}(ẋ), b = Ψ_{T_σ}(ẋ), U = Ψ_G(x).
Before (76) the scrawl '— on' is probably 'on a'.
In (73) the targets look like 'I_ρ' / 'I_σ' in the image (Gothic or script T), but (77) clearly reads T_ρ, T_σ.
